provenance.operatorDescription: Turns a defendant from a person into a legal entity — the organisation shape the model permits and the court-register mappers never expect.
provenance.operatorRationale: YouthDefendantMapper.js:35-37 reads `defendant.personDefendant.personDetails` with no guard whatsoever. `defendant.json` declares personDefendant and legalEntityDefendant as alternative optional properties, so a legal-entity defendant is a payload the producer CAN send. On the legacy it throws a TypeError inside OutboundCourtRegister, which catches it, logs it and returns undefined — the whole hearing's register disappears with no trace. That is the swallowed-failure class this service exists to remove, and it is reachable from an in-contract input, which is what makes it worth a case. A youth legal entity is a nonsense in the domain but not in the schema; the `all` variant is the honest one and the `second-only` variant shows the same loss reached from a hearing that also carries a real child.

operatorDetail.why: a real child first, an organisation second — the register is lost anyway, because the mapper reaches the second entry
